record: STI V2 Release-2 owner-assessed licence decisions LD1-LD6
assessment: Owner-assessed internal compliance decisions with disclosed residual risks. Not an external legal certification and not a special permission from any rights holder.

LD1.decision: The hash-pinned upstream Qt 6.11.2 and pyside-setup 6.11.2 release sources and build scripts are delivered as the Corresponding Source of the unmodified official binaries (D1).
LD1.residual_risk: Exact binding producer-source correspondence is unproven; the binding wheels carry no producer build record.

LD2.decision: In-package source archives plus GPLv3 section 6(d) equivalent access from the download location are the delivery route (D2). Download-only distribution to users' own PCs does not trigger Installation Information (D3).
LD2.residual_risk: The equivalent public access is not operational until it is published with a release.

LD3.decision: Intel's no-reverse-engineering term, scoped in writing to libiomp5md.dll and libiompstubs5md.dll, is compatible with LGPLv3 section 4 for the Qt libraries (D4).
LD3.residual_risk: The scope rests on the written notices; Intel has not confirmed it.

LD4.decision: The two DLLs taken from Intel's pinned, author-signed NuGet package are redistributed under the Intel Simplified Software License (Version October 2022).
LD4.residual_risk: Byte-identical copies also reach the build through PyTorch under the Developer Tools EULA; certificate revocation was not checked.

LD5.decision: intel-openmp/NOTICE.md with the package's copyright line, the full licence text and third-party-programs.txt satisfies the licence's notice condition.
LD5.residual_risk: The licence text itself carries no copyright line.

LD6.decision: The owner accepts the licence's high-risk-use disclaimer. The oneTBB third-party file that third-party-programs.txt refers to is not required.
LD6.residual_risk: The oneTBB finding rests on the upstream oneTBB 2022.3.0 build definition, not on Intel's internal build.
